judged_text: When credential sync is enabled, minimumTokenResponseSchema does not include refresh_token, so the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the parsed data and the calling adapters persist that placeholder into the credential row in the database. GoogleCalendarService (CalendarService.ts ~line 93) and zoom/office365 adapters store {refresh_token: "refresh_token", ...} via prisma.credential.update; any later flow that uses the stored refresh token (e.g. the app is used directly, sync is disabled, or the app is unlinked/relinked) calls the provider's token endpoint with the literal string and the stored credential becomes permanently unusable, forcing re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which when credential sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) validates responses using `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. That schema does not include `refresh_token`, and Zod `z.object(...)` will strip unknown keys, so even if the input had a real `refresh_token`, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` will be missing. The function then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `Office365CalendarService`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is spread into `o365AuthCredentials`, which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with the placeholder and then persist it via `prisma.credential.update`. This matches the finding’s core claim that the placeholder can be stored and break future refresh flows.
